## Control flow statements

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `if` / `else if` / `else` | ✅ | | |
| `while` loop | ✅ | | |
| `do…while` loop | ✅ | | |
| `for (init; cond; update)` | ✅ | | |
| `for…of` over arrays, strings, `Map`, `Set`, and a class implementing `next(): T \| null` | ✅ | • A bare `for (const v of map)` iterates values (use `.keys()` for keys — [ADR-00011](../adr/ADR-00011.md)); the two-name pattern `for (const [k, v] of map)` decomposes entries ([ADR-00481](../adr/ADR-00481.md))<br>• A string iterates per byte, not per Unicode code point — correct for ASCII/Latin-1, the same byte-string narrowing the rest of the string layer carries ([ADR-00535](../adr/ADR-00535.md)) | • The loop variable may be a destructuring pattern (`for (const [a, b] of pairs)` over an array-of-arrays, `for (const { x, y } of points)`), including nested patterns (`for (const [[a, b], c] of …)`) — see [ADR-00192](../adr/ADR-00192.md)/[ADR-00193](../adr/ADR-00193.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stages 1–2<br>• Iterates arrays, a string (its characters, one per byte — [ADR-00535](../adr/ADR-00535.md)), `Map` (values), `Set` (elements), generators, a class implementing `next(): T \| null` ([TDD-00009](../tdd/TDD-00009.md) Stage 1a, a compile-time structural check), **and the spec's real protocol**: a class or object literal with a `[Symbol.iterator]()` returning an iterator whose `next()` yields `{value, done}` — dispatched ahead of the structural shape when both exist ([ADR-00278](../adr/ADR-00278.md)/[ADR-00279](../adr/ADR-00279.md))<br>• A `next(): T \| null` with a non-pointer scalar `T` returns a presence-flagged aggregate ([TDD-00064](../tdd/TDD-00064.md)/[ADR-00199](../adr/ADR-00199.md)), so a legitimately-yielded `0`/`false` does not end iteration; a pointer `T` keeps its null-pointer sentinel — see [ADR-00063](../adr/ADR-00063.md) |
| `for…in` over object keys | ✅ | | |
| `switch` / `case` / `default` / `break` | ✅ | | • Numeric, string, and boolean discriminants |
| `break` / `continue` in loops, including labeled (`outer: for (...) { break outer; }`) | ✅ | | • See [ADR-00010](../adr/ADR-00010.md)<br>• A `break`/`continue` (labeled or not) inside a nested closure/function expression can only target a loop declared within that closure's own body, not one in an enclosing function — a clean compile-time rejection (`break`/`continue` outside of a loop, or an undefined label), not a silent misparse, matching JS's own no-cross-function-boundary label rule ([ADR-00168](../adr/ADR-00168.md)) |
| `return` | ✅ | | • Typed; `void` implicit return handled |
| `throw new Error(msg)` | ✅ | | • Via `setjmp` / `longjmp`<br>• A built-in error constructor is also a first-class *value* (`assert.throws(TypeError, fn)`, `x === RangeError`): a boxed funcref with exact identity, `typeof` `"function"`, native-function stringification ([ADR-00289](../adr/ADR-00289.md)) |
| `try` / `catch` / `finally` | ✅ | • A catch pattern can only destructure the caught value's fixed `{kind, message, name}` shape (every thrown value, including a thrown non-Error primitive, is force-shaped into that one runtime layout), not an arbitrary custom object's own fields, and there's no array-pattern form ([ADR-00170](../adr/ADR-00170.md)) | • Single catch variable, or a destructured object pattern (`catch ({ message, name })`)<br>• `finally` runs on an early `return`/`break`/`continue` (labeled or not), not only on fall-through — the return value is captured before it, a `return` in `finally` overrides, and nested finallys run innermost-first, matching JS ([ADR-00191](../adr/ADR-00191.md)). This holds inside an `async` function and a generator too, including a `finally` that itself `await`s ([ADR-00612](../adr/ADR-00612.md)) |
| Optional catch binding (`try {} catch {}`, no bound param) — ES2019 | ✅ | | • The `(e)` clause is optional — `emit_exceptions.go` already handled an empty `Param` correctly, so this was a parser-only change. See [ADR-00086](../adr/ADR-00086.md) |
| `debugger` statement | ✅ | | • Parsed and erased to a no-op — an AOT-compiled native binary has no attached inspector to break into, matching plain JS with no debugger attached. `debugger` is a reserved word, never a real identifier. See [ADR-00373](../adr/ADR-00373.md) |

| `null` literal | ✅ | | • `T \| null` union type supported |
| `undefined` literal | ✅ | | |

| Arithmetic operators `+ - * / %` | ✅ | | |

| Bitwise operators `& \| ^ ~ << >> >>>` | ✅ | | |
| Assignment operators `+= -= *= /= %= &= \|= ^= <<= >>= >>>=` | ✅ | | |

## Variable declarations

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `const` / `let` / `var` declarations | ✅ | • Definite-assignment analysis is sound-not-complete: a typed `let` assigned only in a maybe-skipped loop or across correlated conditions still falls through to the `undefined`/zero default rather than raising `used before being assigned` ([TDD-00071](../tdd/TDD-00071.md) Stage 2/[ADR-00213](../adr/ADR-00213.md))<br>• A top-level `const`/`let` still isn't readable from a named `function` only in the invariant's genuine edges — a `bigint`, a *scalar*-returning un-annotated call (`emitVarDecl`'s `i64` default), a `new Set([…])` typed from its initializer array, or an init depending on a runtime-local (a `{ …rest }` spread of a destructuring target); an arrow/closure still captures any of them ([TDD-00093](../tdd/TDD-00093.md)) | • A top-level `const`/`let`/`var` is a **module global** — readable and writable from any named `function`, not only a capturing arrow — whenever its type is determinable before `main()` runs: a scalar/string/array/object/`Map`/`Set`, an **un-annotated call to a named function** (`const cfg = loadConfig()`), or an initializer referencing an **earlier global** (`const b = a`). A mutation through it (a reassignment, `arr.push`, `obj.field =`, `map.set`) is seen everywhere, including by a capturing closure ([ADR-00273](../adr/ADR-00273.md)/[TDD-00093](../tdd/TDD-00093.md))<br>• `var` is function-scoped (leaks its enclosing block, and re-declarable with the same name); `let`/`const` are block-scoped; `const` rebinding is rejected<br>• Block-scoped `let`/`const` redeclaration is a compile error; the top-level duplicate check is kind-aware (`var x; var x` allowed, `let x; let x` / `let x; var x` rejected) and the cross-block `let x; { var x }` intersection is caught too — see [TDD-00070](../tdd/TDD-00070.md)/[ADR-00210](../adr/ADR-00210.md)/[ADR-00211](../adr/ADR-00211.md)<br>• A `let`/`const` read before its declaration is a distinct `cannot access 'x' before initialization` TDZ error (including the block-shadowing form) — [TDD-00071](../tdd/TDD-00071.md) Stage 1/[ADR-00212](../adr/ADR-00212.md)<br>• A typed `let` read before assignment is a `used before being assigned` error for the common cases; `var` is exempt — hoisted and zero/`undefined`-initialized, no TDZ ([TDD-00071](../tdd/TDD-00071.md) Stage 2/[ADR-00213](../adr/ADR-00213.md)/[ADR-00454](../adr/ADR-00454.md)) |
| Array destructuring `const [a, b] = arr` | ✅ | • *Assignment* to already-declared targets (`[a, b] = expr`, not a fresh declaration) now reaches declaration-form parity for nesting ([ADR-00595](../adr/ADR-00595.md)): nested array/object patterns (`[[a, b], c] = e`), a trailing `...rest`, and a per-element `= default` (out-of-bounds is the presence signal) all work; a compound operator (`[a, b] += …`) stays rejected, and a member target (`[obj.x, arr[i]] = e`) isn't wired yet | • Holes are supported (`const [, b] = arr` skips index 0)<br>• The source may be a string — `const [a, b] = "xy"` binds its characters (`a`=`"x"`, `b`=`"y"`), one per byte, in both the declaration and assignment forms ([ADR-00536](../adr/ADR-00536.md))<br>• Default values (`[a = 1]`) fire exactly when that position is past the source array's actual length — see [ADR-00157](../adr/ADR-00157.md)/[ADR-00158](../adr/ADR-00158.md)<br>• A rest element (`[a, ...rest]`) works in the declaration form, a destructured parameter, and the assignment form alike — a real, independent copy of every remaining position, empty (not an error) when the source is shorter than the pattern — see [ADR-00161](../adr/ADR-00161.md)<br>• Usable as a for-of loop variable (`for (const [a, b] of pairs)`, over an array-of-arrays), reusing the same unpack core — see [ADR-00192](../adr/ADR-00192.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 1<br>• Nested patterns (`[[a, b], c]`, `[{ x }, { y }]`) work in a declaration, for-of loop variable, and destructured parameter — see [ADR-00193](../adr/ADR-00193.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 2 |
| Object destructuring `const { x, y } = obj` | ✅ | • Default values (`{ x = 1 }`) are supported only for a field typed as a nullable *reference* (`T \| null` where T is string/array/object/class) — the only field shape with a real "not provided" signal; a default on a nullable scalar (`number \| null`, whose `null` is a fake in-band 0 sentinel — [ADR-00158](../adr/ADR-00158.md)) or any non-nullable field is a clean compile-time rejection<br>• *Assignment* to already-declared targets now supports nested patterns (`({ p, q: { r, s } } = obj)`, `({ arr: [x, y] } = obj)`) and object-property defaults, shorthand `{ x = default }` and keyed `{ k: x = default }`, on a nullable-reference field, at declaration-form parity ([ADR-00595](../adr/ADR-00595.md)/[ADR-00597](../adr/ADR-00597.md)); a `= default` on a nested position stays rejected — matching the declaration form<br>• `{ ...rest }` over an `any`/union/generic source (Stage 3c) and in the *assignment* form (`({ a, ...rest } = e)`) stay clean rejections<br>• A computed key (`{ [k]: v }`) is supported only for a **constant** string/number literal key (`{ ["a"]: v }`, `{ [0]: v }` — resolves to that field); a runtime-valued key on a fixed object is a clean rejection ([ADR-00609](../adr/ADR-00609.md)) | • Renaming is supported (`{ x: y }`)<br>• *Assignment* to already-declared targets (`({ x, y } = expr)`, parens required at statement level, matching real JS) — see [ADR-00160](../adr/ADR-00160.md)<br>• Nested patterns (`{ inner: { v }, tag }`, `{ coords: [x, y] }`) work in a declaration, for-of loop variable, and destructured parameter — see [ADR-00193](../adr/ADR-00193.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 2<br>• String- or numeric-literal keys (`{ "k": v }`, `{ 0: v }`) reuse the object-literal key grammar — a non-identifier key has no shorthand, so it must bind through an explicit `: name` ([ADR-00203](../adr/ADR-00203.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 3a)<br>• A rest element (`{ a, ...rest }`) works in the declaration, for-of, and destructured-parameter forms ([ADR-00204](../adr/ADR-00204.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 3b): `rest` binds a fresh residual object of every visible source field not named earlier — a plain object (a class instance's rest strips hidden metadata, matching JS's own-enumerable copy), shallow-copied (a pointer-valued field is shared), usable like any object; requires a statically-known source shape<br>• Usable as a for-of loop variable (`for (const { x, y } of points)`) — see [ADR-00192](../adr/ADR-00192.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 1 |

## Functions & closures

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tagged template literals (`` tag`Hello ${x}` ``) | ✅ | • A **user** tag's `strings` argument has no `.raw` property (this compiler's arrays carry no extra properties) — the built-in `String.raw` tag itself is implemented and interleaves the raw, un-escaped quasis ([ADR-00562](../adr/ADR-00562.md)) | • Desugars to a plain call (`tag(["a","b"], x)`) — interpolated values reach the tag function as real typed values, not implicitly stringified the way a plain template literal's own interpolation is<br>• Any callable — a named function, a class method, or an arrow function/closure (including with a `...rest` parameter) — works as a tag. See [TDD-00059](../tdd/TDD-00059.md)/[ADR-00151](../adr/ADR-00151.md)/[ADR-00152](../adr/ADR-00152.md) |
| Function declarations (top-level) | ✅ | • Cannot reference a sibling top-level binding whose value is a connection handle (`Worker`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`, `BroadcastChannel`/`MessageChannel`, `XMLHttpRequest` — construction opens a thread/socket), a `Promise`, or a generic class instance with **inferred** rather than explicit type arguments (`new Box(5)`, or a nested `new Box<Box<number>>()`) — such a binding stays a `main()` local outside a named function's fresh scope, failing with `undefined variable`. Scalars, strings, arrays, `TypedArray`s, objects, `Map`/`Set`, class instances (including an explicit `new Box<number>()`), the value/event handles (`Blob`, `Date`, `Error`, `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `URLPattern`, `RegExp`, `Headers`, `ArrayBuffer`, `DataView`, `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `Request`, `AbortController`, `Event`/`CustomEvent`, `EventTarget`), and the streams (`ReadableStream`/`WritableStream`/`TransformStream`/`CompressionStream`, the Node streams) + `EventEmitter`, and `http.createServer` handles ([ADR-00426](../adr/ADR-00426.md)) are promoted to module globals and are readable ([TDD-00093](../tdd/TDD-00093.md)/[ADR-00342](../adr/ADR-00342.md)); arrow functions/closures capture everything regardless ([TDD-00057](../tdd/TDD-00057.md))<br>• A genuinely circular pair of mutually-recursive unannotated functions can't converge on a return type and keeps the scalar-default fallback ([TDD-00058](../tdd/TDD-00058.md))<br>• The `arguments` object is synthesized from the declared parameters when they all share one type ([ADR-00387](../adr/ADR-00387.md)) — `.length`, indexing, and `for…of` work; mixed-type parameters, a rest/destructured parameter, and an arrow function (which has no own `arguments` in JS) are clean rejections, and it reflects the declared parameters rather than growing with extra untyped arguments (there is no variadic call beyond an explicit `...rest`); class method bodies get the same synthesis ([ADR-00464](../adr/ADR-00464.md)) | • Named, typed params, typed return<br>• A leading `this` parameter (`function f(this: T, …)`) — TS's explicit-`this` typing form — is parsed and erased, exactly as real TS erases it at emit; the remaining parameters bind by their real positions ([ADR-00373](../adr/ADR-00373.md)) |
| Arrow functions / lambdas | ✅ | | • Full closures; captures via heap-allocated env struct<br>• An arrow inside a class method captures the enclosing lexical `this` like any other variable (nested arrows included; a `function(){}` body keeps its own dynamic `this` and stays a clean rejection) ([ADR-00460](../adr/ADR-00460.md)) |
| Function expressions (`var f = function(x) {...}`, callback arguments, IIFE bodies) | ✅ | • A generic function used by value is out of scope (no single monomorphized symbol to point at) ([ADR-00200](../adr/ADR-00200.md)) | • Anonymous and named. A named function expression (`var f = function fact(n) {...}`) binds its own name inside its own body — for self-reference/recursion — without leaking to the enclosing scope, via a synthetic self-capture whose env cell holds the closure's own header ([ADR-00178](../adr/ADR-00178.md)). This holds even when the name shadows a *top-level function* of the same name: the resolver binds the expression's name in its own scope before rewriting the body, so the self-reference stays the expression while outer calls still reach the top-level function ([ADR-00601](../adr/ADR-00601.md))<br>• `async function(...) {...}` expressions are supported<br>• An IIFE runs inline — `(function(){…})()`, `(() => …)()`, and a named recursive IIFE `(function fact(n){…})(5)` alike — via the general function-value call path<br>• Reuses arrow functions' closure machinery — same captures, same heap-allocated env struct. See [TDD-00060](../tdd/TDD-00060.md)/[ADR-00168](../adr/ADR-00168.md) |
| Default parameter values | ✅ | • A default expression may reference an earlier *scalar/string* parameter — `function f(a: number, b: number = a * 2)`, including chaining (`c = b + 1`) — for a free function, an instance method, a static method, and a constructor (including a parameter-property ctor `constructor(public x = 1, public y = x)`) ([ADR-00598](../adr/ADR-00598.md)/[ADR-00599](../adr/ADR-00599.md)); the earlier param's passed value (or its own default) is bound only while the default is evaluated, so an argument still sees the caller's scope. An earlier param of **any** supported kind is referenceable — scalar/string, *array* (`b = a.length`, `a[i]` — [ADR-00610](../adr/ADR-00610.md)), and *nullable-scalar* (`b = (a ?? 0) + 1` — [ADR-00611](../adr/ADR-00611.md)) — across free functions, instance/static methods, and constructors; a rest-parameter constructor is unsupported | |
| Optional parameters (`param?`) | ✅ | • An omitted `?` argument gets the parameter type's zero value — the same `undefined` stand-in default parameter values/destructuring defaults use, not real JS's `undefined` ([ADR-00164](../adr/ADR-00164.md)) | |
| Rest parameters (`...args: number[]`) | ✅ | | • Works on named function declarations, class methods, arrow functions/closures, and **function type annotations** (`(...xs: number[]) => R`, `(head: number, ...tail: number[]) => R`, and the same as a `type` alias) alike. See [ADR-00151](../adr/ADR-00151.md)/[ADR-00152](../adr/ADR-00152.md)/[ADR-00385](../adr/ADR-00385.md) |
| Destructured function parameters (`function f({ x, y }: T) {}` / `function f([a, b]: T[]) {}`) | ✅ | • Requires an explicit type annotation on the pattern (no sensible unannotated default the way a scalar param has); no combination with `...` or a whole-parameter default value<br>• A `= default` on a nested position is a clean rejection; per-element defaults follow the same rules as the statement-level destructuring rows | • Each individual pattern element/field may have its own default (`function f([a = 1]: number[])`, `function f({ x = "d" }: T)`)<br>• Nested patterns (`function f([[a, b]]: number[][])`, `function f({ p: { x } }: T)`) work — see [ADR-00193](../adr/ADR-00193.md)/[TDD-00065](../tdd/TDD-00065.md) Stage 2<br>• Works on named function declarations, class methods/constructors, and arrow functions alike — including an array-destructured param on an arrow function/closure, since array-typed closure parameters are supported ([ADR-00152](../adr/ADR-00152.md)). See [ADR-00109](../adr/ADR-00109.md)/[ADR-00158](../adr/ADR-00158.md) |
| Nested function declarations (`function outer() { function inner() {...}; return inner(); }`) | ✅ | • A declaration inside a lexical block (an `if`/`for`/`while`/`do-while`/bare block, a `try`/`catch`/`finally` block, or a `switch` case) is supported and block-scoped ([TDD-00152](../tdd/TDD-00152.md)/[ADR-00602](../adr/ADR-00602.md)); the residual is the specialized `for…of`/`for…in` iterator variants (generator/stream/`Symbol.iterator` paths) that iterate their body directly (no miscompile — capturing such a loop variable is a clean rejection)<br>• A block-nested declaration capturing a **C-style `for` loop variable** is a clean rejection — the loop variable is a single per-iteration cell; copy it to a `const` inside the loop body and capture that ([ADR-00602](../adr/ADR-00602.md))<br>• Captures enclosing locals/parameters (by reference, emitted as a closure value — [TDD-00129](../tdd/TDD-00129.md) Stage 1/[ADR-00386](../adr/ADR-00386.md)), but only for use **at or after** the declaration point — a capturing nested function called before its declaration is a clean error (full pre-declaration hoisting is Stage 2); a non-capturing one keeps full hoisting/forward-reference. Capturing an array variable, and a capturing nested *generator*, stay clean rejections<br>• Generic (`<T>`) nested declarations and same-scope duplicate names are clean compile errors ([TDD-00057](../tdd/TDD-00057.md)/[ADR-00149](../adr/ADR-00149.md)) | • Hoisted, forward-referenceable, self-recursive, visible to its own further-nested descendants |
| `Function.prototype.call` / `.apply` / `.bind` | ✅ | • `thisArg` is evaluated then **ignored** — a closure has no rebindable `this`, so method-borrowing (calling a method value against a different receiver) is unsupported; only the arguments are forwarded<br>• Only on a first-class function **value** (a closure, function parameter, arrow/function expression, or named function) — call/apply/bind on a built-in (`net.connect.apply(…)`) isn't supported, since built-ins aren't function values<br>• `.apply` takes either a literal array (`f.apply(null, [a, b])`) or a runtime array spread into a **rest** parameter (`f.apply(null, arr)` where `f` is `(...xs) => …`); a runtime array into a fixed-arity function is the usual spread-into-fixed-arity rejection<br>• `.bind` is V1-scoped to functions whose parameters are plain scalar/string/pointer types with no rest slot — an array/nullable-scalar/rest parameter is a clean compile error | • `f.call(thisArg, a, b)` / `f.apply(thisArg, [a, b])` lower to a direct `f(a, b)`; `f.apply(thisArg, arr)` spreads into the rest slot; `f.bind(thisArg, …bound)` builds a new partially-applied closure (a trampoline capturing `f` + bound args). All type-checked against `f`'s parameters exactly as a normal call ([TDD-00137](../tdd/TDD-00137.md)) |
| Function overload signatures (`function f(x: number): number;` + impl) | ✅ | • Signatures are parsed and **erased** — call sites type-check against the implementation's parameter list only, with no per-signature arity/type narrowing (an ill-formed group — a signature with no implementation, interrupted, or name-mismatched — is still a clean rejection) | • Top-level `function` groups, class methods, and constructor overloads ([ADR-00446](../adr/ADR-00446.md)); only the implementation is compiled |
| Generator functions (`function* f(): T { yield x; }`, `.next(value)`, `for...of`) | ✅ | • A free `function*` may be top-level **or nested** (a nested `function*` captures enclosing state by reference — an enclosing `let` mutated after the generator is created is seen by a later `.next()` — reusing the closure-boxing on the instance's `__env`; an *array* capture stays a clean rejection); a generator *expression* is supported only as a top-level `const/let/var G = function* ...` binding (rewritten to a named declaration, [TDD-00096](../tdd/TDD-00096.md)/[ADR-00293](../adr/ADR-00293.md)) — an argument/nested/IIFE use is a clean rejection. Instance generator methods — sync and `async *m()` — are supported separately (rows below), but `static`/`abstract` generator methods stay clean rejections ([TDD-00094](../tdd/TDD-00094.md))<br>• The return-type annotation is optional — the element type is inferred from the body's yields (numeric join, `yield*` delegation, return fallback; only a genuinely non-joinable mix still requires the annotation — [ADR-00293](../adr/ADR-00293.md)); still requires a plain non-destructured parameter list and a non-array element/parameter type (a tuple/object element type works)<br>• Calling `.next()` again after completion returns `{value: <T's zero value>, done: true}` — this compiler's usual stand-in for real JS's `undefined` ([TDD-00061](../tdd/TDD-00061.md)/[ADR-00173](../adr/ADR-00173.md)) | • Real suspend/resume via this compiler's own `ucontext.h`-based fiber primitive (the same one `http.listen`/`await fetch(...)` already use), not a synchronous stand-in — see [ADR-00171](../adr/ADR-00171.md)/[ADR-00172](../adr/ADR-00172.md)<br>• The full iterator protocol: `.throw(e)` injects at the suspension point (a body `try/catch` handles it, else it propagates to the caller and finishes the generator), `.return(v)` completes the generator running enclosing `finally` blocks, and `yield*` delegates to an inner generator — forwarding sent values / `.throw()` / `.return()` and evaluating to the inner's return value ([ADR-00259](../adr/ADR-00259.md)/[TDD-00086](../tdd/TDD-00086.md)). A `return` inside a `try/finally` runs the `finally`<br>• Leaving a `for...of` over a generator early closes the iterator — a `break`, a `return` from the loop body, and an outer labeled `break`/`continue` all drive the suspended generator's `.return()`, so an enclosing `finally` in the generator body runs (interleaved innermost-first with any body/consumer `finally`), matching JS ([ADR-00613](../adr/ADR-00613.md)/[ADR-00614](../adr/ADR-00614.md)); a `throw` propagating out of the body is the one path that doesn't yet close it (exceptions unwind through a separate mechanism) |

## Async / Promise

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `async` functions | ✅ | | • **Every** async fn returns a real task-shaped `Promise<T>`: a fn containing an `await` runs on a ucontext fiber (so it can yield at every await); a no-`await` one settles inline. No `libcurl` linked unless `fetch` is used ([TDD-00084](../tdd/TDD-00084.md) Part A / [ADR-00249](../adr/ADR-00249.md)/[ADR-00268](../adr/ADR-00268.md))<br>• Nullable-scalar, destructured, **and rest** parameters in a genuinely-suspending fn are all marshalled through the coroutine task's args bundle — a rest param's trailing args pack into an array that binds like any other array param ([TDD-00084](../tdd/TDD-00084.md) Part C / [ADR-00256](../adr/ADR-00256.md))<br>• Named `async function` declarations, `async (...) => ...` arrows, and async function expressions all supported |
| `await` expressions | ✅ | | • A Promise is a **reusable value** — `await p` twice returns the same result, and a member is readable after a combinator; `await` reads the slot without freeing it, including a raw-fetch `Promise<Response>` (its pending struct is never freed and `__kml_await_fetch` short-circuits an already-done handle) ([ADR-00270](../adr/ADR-00270.md)/[TDD-00090](../tdd/TDD-00090.md))<br>• Every `await` yields a microtask tick — of an already-settled promise **and of a non-promise value** (`await 1` defers the continuation exactly as JS does; identity in value only) — and the resume is a microtask ordered in FIFO with `.then`/`queueMicrotask` (matches JS: `f(); log("c")` where `f` awaits prints `a c b`) ([ADR-00268](../adr/ADR-00268.md)/[TDD-00088](../tdd/TDD-00088.md), [ADR-00281](../adr/ADR-00281.md)); inside an *async generator body* an await parks the step itself ([ADR-00283](../adr/ADR-00283.md))<br>• Registers a resume reaction on the promise and parks; on `fetch()`'s `Promise<Response>` it really waits ([ADR-00050](../adr/ADR-00050.md)); an explicitly `: Promise<T>`-annotated variable, a plain function returning `new Promise`, and an `async` fn returning a promise all `await` correctly ([ADR-00265](../adr/ADR-00265.md)) |
| `Promise.all` / `.race` / `.allSettled` | ✅ | | • A member Promise is a **reusable value**: the combinator reads each slot without freeing it, so any member — a value/task promise **or** a raw-fetch `Promise<Response>` — can be awaited again or read after the combinator ([ADR-00270](../adr/ADR-00270.md)/[TDD-00090](../tdd/TDD-00090.md))<br>• `.race`/`.any` over `setTimeout`-based task promises return the shortest-delay member — `__kml_timer_fire_next` fires strictly earliest-due and the waiter list wakes the awaiter event-driven ([ADR-00266](../adr/ADR-00266.md))<br>• Real concurrency over `Array<Promise<Response>>` (fetch) **and** over `Array<Promise<T>>` from may-suspend async fns ([TDD-00083](../tdd/TDD-00083.md) Stage 2); only a genuinely-already-resolved array collapses to a synchronous collect<br>• A rejecting task member rejects `.all`/`.race` (re-thrown at the `await`) and reports `rejected` in `.allSettled` (fiber-safe exceptions, [ADR-00244](../adr/ADR-00244.md))<br>• `.race`/`.any` over task promises wait via an event-driven waiter list (a settling member wakes the awaiter), not a busy poll ([ADR-00266](../adr/ADR-00266.md)) |
| `Promise.any` | ✅ | | • Over task promises it skips rejected members and resolves to the first *fulfilled* one; when every member rejects it throws a real `AggregateError` carrying each reason on `.errors` ([ADR-00248](../adr/ADR-00248.md))<br>• Over `Array<Promise<Response>>` (raw fetches) it settles to the first transport-successful response and throws an `AggregateError` only when every fetch fails at the transport level — an HTTP 404/500 is a fulfilled fetch, per WHATWG ([ADR-00251](../adr/ADR-00251.md)/[TDD-00084](../tdd/TDD-00084.md) Part C) |
| `Promise.resolve` / `Promise.reject` | ✅ | | • Both build a settled *task* promise, so `await` / `.then` / `.catch` / `.finally` and `Promise.all`/`.any`/`.race` arrays all work. `Promise.resolve(v)` fulfils with `v` (an already-promise arg flattens through, no-arg is `Promise<void>`); `Promise.reject(e)` rejects with the error (a bare primitive wrapped like a thrown value) — no fiber/libcurl linked ([ADR-00262](../adr/ADR-00262.md))<br>• `Promise.reject(e)` is typed `Promise<never>`, so a rejected value assigns to any binding — `const s: string = await Promise.reject(...)` type-checks (the value is dead, `await` re-throws) ([ADR-00264](../adr/ADR-00264.md)) |
| `new Promise((resolve, reject) => …)` (executor constructor) | ✅ | | • **Thenable adoption**: `resolve(anotherPromise)` settles the outer promise with the inner's value (or reason) when the inner settles — reaction-based, so it's a microtask tick like `.then`, not synchronous ([ADR-00271](../adr/ADR-00271.md)/[TDD-00091](../tdd/TDD-00091.md)). Only a typed `Promise` argument adopts; a custom duck-typed `{ then }` object isn't adopted (this compiler has no `PromiseLike<T>` type — it's a clean type mismatch, not a silent miss)<br>• Synchronous resolve/reject, conditional settle, and **first-settle-wins** (a later resolve/reject is ignored); `.then`/`.catch`/`await` all work ([ADR-00263](../adr/ADR-00263.md)/[TDD-00087](../tdd/TDD-00087.md))<br>• The executor may be an arrow, a `function(…) {…}` expression, a closure-typed variable, or a bare top-level-function reference ([ADR-00267](../adr/ADR-00267.md))<br>• **Deferred** resolution from a `setTimeout` callback (`new Promise((res) => setTimeout(() => res(v), ms))`) — awaiting drives the microtask queue and fires due timers until it settles<br>• Works returned across a function boundary too — a plain function or an `async` fn returning `new Promise(...)` (the `delay()` helper pattern), via async-return flattening ([ADR-00265](../adr/ADR-00265.md)); `T` from `new Promise<T>`, default `number` |
| `Promise.prototype.then` / `.catch` / `.finally` + `queueMicrotask` | ✅ | | • `.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` directly on a raw fetch `Promise<Response>` never blocks the synchronous script: the transport wait is deferred to a queued microtask that settles a bridge promise at event-loop drain ([ADR-00280](../adr/ADR-00280.md), replacing [ADR-00258](../adr/ADR-00258.md)'s synchronous drive); the fetch promise stays a reusable value (`p.then(f)` + `await p` in either order share one transfer)<br>• A missing/`undefined`/`null` callback slot is a pass-through, as in JS — `p.then()` chains the source value, `.then(undefined, onR)` is the `.catch` shape ([ADR-00281](../adr/ADR-00281.md))<br>• The callback runs as a microtask when the promise settles and its result **chains** into the returned promise — `p.then(f).then(g)` passes `f`'s result to `g`, `.catch` recovers, `.finally` passes through ([ADR-00248](../adr/ADR-00248.md)); a `.catch` error param is the error object with or without annotation ([ADR-00255](../adr/ADR-00255.md))<br>• `await`ing a chain result (`await p.then(f)`) waits for the chain's microtask ([ADR-00262](../adr/ADR-00262.md)); works on any async fn's result and directly on a raw fetch `Promise<Response>` (4xx/5xx fulfils, transport failure rejects — [ADR-00258](../adr/ADR-00258.md))<br>• `queueMicrotask` is a FIFO drained after the synchronous script and before timers |
| Async generators (`async function*`, `async *m()`) | ✅ | | • **V8/spec step timing** ([ADR-00283](../adr/ADR-00283.md), node-diff verified): `.next()` starts the body *synchronously* up to the first `await`/`yield`; an `await` inside the body **parks the step** (its `Promise<{value,done}>` stays pending, the consumer's script continues, the settle re-enters the fiber as a microtask — so body side effects interleave with consumer-side microtasks exactly as node's do, and `await <plain value>` in a body defers one tick); `.next`/`.throw`/`.return` during an in-flight step **queue** (AsyncGeneratorEnqueue) and are serviced in order when it settles — `Promise.all`-style double-`.next()` and a `.return()` whose `finally` awaits both work<br>• Top-level **or nested** `async function*`, and a class `async *m()` method (a nested one captures enclosing state by reference on the instance's `__env`; an array capture is a clean rejection) ([ADR-00274](../adr/ADR-00274.md))<br>• `.next()` returns a real `Promise<{value,done}>` — settled when the body reached a `yield`/completion synchronously, genuinely *pending* while the body is parked at an `await` ([ADR-00275](../adr/ADR-00275.md)'s settle-through-`__kml_promise_settle` rule, [ADR-00283](../adr/ADR-00283.md)'s step model)<br>• `yield*` delegates to another generator **or** a user `Symbol.asyncIterator` async iterable inside an async generator (awaiting + re-yielding each element); a `.throw(e)`/`.return(v)` on the outer at an async-iterable `yield*` **delegates into the inner iterator's own `.throw`/`.return`** when it has them (the inner may catch a throw and keep yielding, or run its own cleanup), else runs the outer's own propagate/complete path ([ADR-00274](../adr/ADR-00274.md)/[ADR-00275](../adr/ADR-00275.md)/[ADR-00276](../adr/ADR-00276.md))<br> • Fuses the sync-generator fiber with the coroutine-task scheduler park ([ADR-00253](../adr/ADR-00253.md)/[ADR-00254](../adr/ADR-00254.md)): the body both `yield`s to its consumer and `await`s (a `fetch` busy-spins, a task promise drives the scheduler), a throw rejects the outstanding `.next()`, and a method binds `this` from the receiver<br>• The full protocol: `.throw(e)` / `.return(v)` ([ADR-00260](../adr/ADR-00260.md)) and `yield*` over an inner async generator — each inner step's promise awaited, forwarding sent values / `.throw()` / `.return()` ([ADR-00261](../adr/ADR-00261.md)/[TDD-00086](../tdd/TDD-00086.md)) — the same isolated-swap machinery the sync generators use, settling the returned promise (fulfilled if a body `try/catch` handles the throw or the return runs its finallys, rejected on an uncaught throw) ([ADR-00260](../adr/ADR-00260.md)/[TDD-00086](../tdd/TDD-00086.md)) |
| `for await...of` (async iteration) | ✅ | | • Consumes an async-generator instance, a user class implementing the async-iteration protocol by hand — a `[Symbol.asyncIterator]()` returning an iterator whose `async next(): Promise<{value,done}>` is awaited each turn (`return this` self-iterators and separate iterator objects both work) ([ADR-00269](../adr/ADR-00269.md)/[TDD-00089](../tdd/TDD-00089.md)) — an **object literal** carrying `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` (arrow-valued or method shorthand, returning an async/sync generator or a class iterator; captures via the closure, since object-literal methods have no `this`) ([ADR-00279](../adr/ADR-00279.md)), **or any sync iterable the sync `for...of` takes**, awaiting each element: an array (a promise element awaits to its value — including a raw fetch `Promise<Response>` element, built to its `Response` — a rejected element propagates and stops the loop, a plain value awaits as identity), a `Map` (values) / `Set` (elements), a sync generator, and a `[Symbol.iterator]()` class or object literal ([ADR-00272](../adr/ADR-00272.md)/[TDD-00092](../tdd/TDD-00092.md), [ADR-00277](../adr/ADR-00277.md)/[ADR-00278](../adr/ADR-00278.md))<br>• Awaits each `.next()` promise (re-throwing a rejected step) before reading `.done`/`.value` ([ADR-00253](../adr/ADR-00253.md)/[TDD-00085](../tdd/TDD-00085.md)); the loop is a suspension point in itself — an enclosing async fn parks at the first element even when nothing else in it awaits, so the top-level script continues first, as in JS ([ADR-00281](../adr/ADR-00281.md))<br>• A destructuring loop variable (`for await (const { x, y } of …)`, `const [a, b]` over a tuple element) unpacks each element in the body, reusing the sync for-of destructuring core ([ADR-00257](../adr/ADR-00257.md)) |

A class-typed variable whose static class is `T` itself or an ancestor of `T` folds to a compile-time constant; one whose static class is an *ancestor* of the right-hand class (e.g. `const s: Shape = new Circle(...); s instanceof Circle`) needs a real runtime tag read. See [ADR-00067](../adr/ADR-00067.md)/[ADR-00083](../adr/ADR-00083.md)<br>• `instanceof` against five built-in types (`Array`, `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, `RegExp`) is a compile-time constant off the already-known static type ([ADR-00162](../adr/ADR-00162.md)); `instanceof` against `Error`/`TypeError`/etc. is a separate, sibling mechanism keyed off a different hidden tag (see the `Error` subtypes row above and [TDD-00013](../tdd/TDD-00013.md))<br>• `x instanceof Object` is a compile-time constant computed by *negating* the closed set of primitive types (number/string/boolean/bigint/symbol/null/undefined) — true for every non-primitive (class instance, object, array, function, `Date`, `Map`/`Set`, `RegExp`, …), false for a primitive ([ADR-00605](../adr/ADR-00605.md)) |

## Known limitations

- **Strict-mode early errors**: there's no general strict-mode parser context, so several Test262 early-error cases around a literal `"use strict"` directive stay unrejected — notably `eval`/`arguments` as an *assignment* target in strict code, and bindings inside a getter/setter accessor body. A narrower safe subset is caught: duplicate parameter names, a non-simple parameter list, and `eval`/`arguments` as a parameter or `let`/`const`/`var` (or for-of/for-in loop-variable) binding name under `"use strict"` (or an always-strict class method). Block-scope `let`/`const`-vs-`var` redeclaration *is* tracked — a strict-independent early error, including the cross-nested-block `let x; { var x }` intersection (see [TDD-00070](../tdd/TDD-00070.md)/[ADR-00210](../adr/ADR-00210.md)/[ADR-00211](../adr/ADR-00211.md)).
